text:
jessica-plat: Heads up — trace storage rates spiked ~3x last week. We need a pragmatic plan to prune low-value spans without killing debuggability. Thoughts on span-priority + age-based expiration + a clear rehydrate path? :thinking:

sam-infra: Agree. Raw idea: keep full traces for 21d, produce aggregated rollups for the next 180d (span counts, error flags, key tags), then ultra-cold compressed blobs for 1y. Rehydrate via async on-demand. Cuts storage costs a lot.

priya-ml: Concern: aggressive rollups lose stack/context we rely on for incident RCA. Alternate: error-first retention — keep full traces for any errored request or latency > p95 for 60d; non-error traces sampled heavily after 7d. Keeps signal for ML/alerts.

tom-sre: Also needs per-environment defaults. prod should retain more; staging/dev can be aggressive. And add per-team quotas so cost is accountable.

katie-pm: From UX POV the console needs to show expected rehydrate cost and ETA before a user triggers cold rehydrate. Also surface current sample rates and "what was pruned" in that window.

jessica-plat: Good call. How do we keep fast lookups for trace_id/service queries on older windows?

sam-infra: Keep a tiny persistent index: trace_id -> tier pointer + minimal metadata for 365d. Index should be ~5-12% of raw and fit on cheap SSDs. Then lookups can kick off rehydrate jobs.

priya-ml: Also propose preserving full traces longer for the top contributors to errors (rolling top 1% of services), so our anomaly models don't degrade.

tom-sre: Can we make policy rules flexible? Example: keep when tag:error OR (latency_ms > 2000) OR (span.op == db.query AND cardinality < 100).

jessica-plat: Yes — we could expose a small policy DSL in the exporter config. PoC config for discussion:

```exporter:
  retention_policy:
    - when: "error == true"
      keep: 90d
    - when: "latency_ms > 2000"
      keep: 60d
    - when: "span.op == 'db.query' and span.cardinality < 100"
      keep: 30d
    - default:
      sample: 0.01
      keep: 7d
```

sam-infra: That DSL looks actionable. Implementation note: evaluation must be cheap at ingestion — we can't add a slow eval step on the hot path. Consider compile-to-bytecode or precompiled matchers.

katie-pm: Also add a temporary "rehydrate budget" per team so on-call can raise retention during incidents without permanent cost changes. Show budget usage in console.

priya-ml: Plus, aggregated rollups should retain fingerprints and error histograms so ML detectors and trend pipelines keep working even if raw spans are gone.

ops-bot: snapshot-backup: daily snapshot completed 2026-03-19T02:00Z :white_check_mark:

jessica-plat: Next steps: Sam to spike policy DSL and index size estimates; Priya to define error-preservation heuristics and ML needs; Tom to draft per-env quota plan; I'll mock console rehydrate UX. Ping me with blockers. :thumbsup:

tom-sre: ack

sam-infra: starting a spike, will share numbers by EOD Thu

priya-ml: adding heuristics doc to drive tests

katie-pm: will add UX story to backlog
